notes: Paper match: arXiv 1703.04803 = Golovich et al. 2017 ApJ 838, 110 (DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/aa667f). Pointer: Table 4 (offsets between components, kpc) matches; absolute positions are in Table 3; Fig. 9 = red-sequence luminosity map matches; positions are discussed in §4.3 (4.3.1 galaxy distribution, 4.3.2 mass distribution) rather than §4.1-4.2 of the arXiv numbering. Fig. 10 = WL mass map with 1-sigma peak error bars; Fig. 11 = bootstrap peak locations (68%/95% contours). All four proxies (WL peak, X-ray peak, red-sequence luminosity peak, BCG) have absolute coordinates; WL, X-ray and luminosity peaks have asymmetric per-axis bootstrap errors; RA errors are printed in seconds of time (1 s of RA = 9.12 arcsec at Dec +52.57 deg). No luminosity-weighted CENTROID is tabulated (only a luminosity-map peak), so the protocol S fallback is the east BCG, which has no stated positional uncertainty. Table 4 offsets are bootstrap estimates and differ from separations computed from the Table 3 point positions (my computation using the paper's 115 kpc/arcmin: I-G ~313 kpc (163 arcsec), I-Lum ~183 kpc (95.5 arcsec), I-BCG ~268 kpc (140 arcsec), BCG-G ~483 kpc, Lum-G ~411 kpc). Internal inconsistency: §5.1 says the east gas core is offset 'from the BCG in the east by ~320 kpc (see Table 4)', but Table 4 BCG--ICM East = 480±5.0 kpc and DM--ICM East = 319 kpc; the 320-kpc text figure seems to correspond to DM--ICM. §4.3.2 text: 'This is due to the BCG sitting ~300 kpc east of the mass peak.' Abstract: 'We do not find significant offsets between dark matter and galaxies, but the uncertainties are large with the current lensing data.'
